newsitem.title: USA: Immunex says arthritis drug safe in trial.
newsitem.headline: Immunex says arthritis drug safe in trial.

text.p: Immunex Corp said Tuesday its drug Enbrel, a TNF Receptor that can be used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, was shown to be safe in a multi-center retreatment study.

"These data are exciting because they support the efficacy we have seen to date and at the same time show that the drug can be given safely over a longer period of time," Dr. Larry Moreland, the principal investigator, said in a statement.
The test data were presented in Singapore at a medical conference.

The open-label trial is designed to measure the long-term safety of Enbrel in 106 rheumatoid arthritis patients. All patients had previously received the drug for a maximum three months in earlier trials but had stopped when the trial ended. Symptoms in those patients subsequently recurred.
In the current study, clinical improvement was defined by at least 20 percent improvement in tender and swollen joints.

At six months, 82 percent of patients showed improvement in swollen joints and 88 percent in tender joints. Eleven patients received Enbrel for one year, and 91 percent achieved a 20 percent improvement in swollen and painful joints.

The drug was generally well tolerated. Injection site reactions were relatively mild and infrequent, occurring in two percent of all injections. No antibodies against the drug were found in patients tested to date.
